items.title: Nvidia's SoL-Pi system cuts coding agent token usage nearly in half by optimizing the harness
items.summary: SoL-Pi cuts coding agents' token usage by up to 49 percent with little change in performance by optimizing the control layer between the model and its environment. A research agent tested 152 approaches across more than 3,000 runs to develop the system, though the gains were smaller on other benchmarks. The article Nvidia's SoL-Pi system cuts coding agent token usage nearly in half by optimizing the harness appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can now tell you exactly where you screwed up your IKEA shelf
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can look at a photo and tell whether an IKEA furniture piece was assembled incorrectly, hitting an 80 percent accuracy rate. Back in November 2025, the best model managed just 28 percent. According to Epoch AI, the speed isn't quite fast enough yet for real-time assembly guidance, but the gap is closing quickly. items.title: OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data
items.summary: OpenAI has shared new details from its ongoing AI safety investigation. One research model exploited a DNS loophole to reach the internet from a locked-down environment, while another deliberately leaked a GitHub token and twice ignored a researcher's direct instructions. items.title: Pentagon was right to slap Anthropic with a security supply chain risk label, federal court says
items.summary: A federal appeals court has upheld the Pentagon's decision to bar Anthropic from military contracts. Defense Secretary Hegseth argues the company's safety restrictions could jeopardize military operations. Anthropic says the designation has already cost it billions. The article Pentagon was right to slap Anthropic with a security supply chain risk label, federal court says appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Another Google Deepmind researcher quits, says building superintelligent AI soon is "inherently irresponsible"
items.summary: Google Deepmind researcher Robert O'Callahan has quit, saying AI's "current rate of change is far too high." He worked on chip design tools that helped make AI cheaper and faster, a contribution he can no longer justify. Many colleagues share his concerns but rarely speak out, he says. The article Another Google Deepmind researcher quits, says building superintelligent AI soon is "inherently irresponsible" appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Microsoft gives Copilot another makeover, adding an Autopilot agent and usage-based billing
items.summary: Microsoft is splitting its Copilot app into three sections: Home, Code, and a new agent called "Autopilot." Built on OpenClaw, the agent runs continuously in the cloud, where it can monitor Teams channels and complete tasks on its own, according to Microsoft. items.title: Meta's Muse agent gives every user a full cloud computer running Ubuntu Linux
items.summary: Meta gives every Muse user a free cloud computer running Ubuntu Linux where they can install software, write code, and browse the web. A "Sentinel" process monitors sensitive actions outside the user's workspace, while users can inspect every file in the system. With over 500,000 users in its first week, Meta is betting on product reach over model power. The article Meta's Muse agent gives every user a full cloud computer running Ubuntu Linux app

items.title: Intelligence doesn't come cheap as AI drives up costs for the NSA, hospitals, and insurers
items.summary: The NSA is already spending billions of dollars to test advanced AI models, mostly on computing power, according to The Washington Sun. Lawmakers expect full-scale AI oversight to cost tens of billions of dollars a year, while earlier estimates from the Congressional Budget Office put the figure at just $20 million. items.title: Google's "Call for Me" lets Gemini phone businesses for you
items.summary: Google is testing "Call for Me," a feature that lets Gemini call businesses on a user's behalf. The article Google's "Call for Me" lets Gemini phone businesses for you appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Anthropic signs $11.6 billion cloud deal with Akamai, pushing its compute spending past $500 billion in under a year
items.summary: Anthropic has reportedly signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud deal with Akamai Technologies and will receive a warrant for up to 5 percent of Akamai's shares. Its compute deals have reportedly totaled $517 billion in 11 months. CEO Dario Amodei has warned that Anthropic could go bankrupt if its revenue forecasts are even slightly off.
